chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Coda recordings under Rene Hernandez's name; "Killer Joe" and "No Noise"
summary: Verne-contracted, the band recorded for Coda as the Rene Hernandez orchestra; John Bartee wrote "No Noise" from his baby's crying.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see. . . You were on contract to Verne records at the time. Coda released records under the name of the Rene Hernandez orchestra; in reality, it was the Machito orchestra because you were on contract too. Those recordings made with Coda, did the entire band play under the name of Rene Hernandez?
Do you remember a tune called 'Killer Joe'?
Okay, because later on it became "No Noise" - Part I & II, same melody and everything. What inspired "No Noise", was that - was it "Killer Joe" with the bop phrases in there or was it something else?
Well, that number - that particular number - was John Bartee original form.

John Bartee, and he made that because when he was trying to arrange, in his house, he had a little baby and the little baby, Joe, was breaking things, making noise, crying, and he was very gentle, he is a very gentle, he used to say: "Please, please, please, don't make no noise"; so from that particular atmosphere or whatever, he wrote that number, "No Noise".
Oh! the phrase "No Noise" he got it while he was telling his child - children - not to make any noise?
